subject: Error in ldsc function and query r.e. variable quantity

messages.author: 3f995153570fdbff
messages.subject: Error in ldsc function and query r.e. variable quantity
parts:
Hi,

I'm currently trying to run a large EFA analysis in GenomicSEM with a lot of traits (121). I've previously run the same analysis (only had 33 traits included that time) and that all worked absolutely fine.

This time I get an error at the end of the ldsc function when I run:

LDSCoutput <- ldsc(traits, sample.prev, population.prev,ld,wld,trait.names = TRUE)

It runs all the analysis but at the end comes up with the following error:

Error in dimnames(x) <- dn : 
  length of 'dimnames' [2] not equal to array extent

> ##optional command to save the ldsc output in case you want to use it in a later R session. 
> save(LDSCoutput, file= "EFA_all_traits_LDSC.RData")

Error in save(LDSCoutput, file = "EFA_all_traits_LDSC.RData") : 
  object ‘LDSCoutput’ not found
> LDSCoutput
Error: object 'LDSCoutput' not found

The only two differences to what I did previously was that here I wrote 'trait.names = TRUE' into the code rather than simply 'trait.names':

LDSCoutput <- ldsc(traits, sample.prev, population.prev,ld,wld,trait.names)

I changed it because if I tried running the code this way it no longer works for either of my analyses because this error crops up:

Error in file(paste0(log2, "_ldsc.log"), open = "wt") : 
  cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In file(paste0(log2, "_ldsc.log"), open = "wt") :
  cannot open file [file of trait names... e.g. SUBJECTIVE_WELLBEING_INSOMNIA_SLEEP_DURATION_SNORING_DAYTIME_DOZING_MORNINGNESS_[... truncated]]

It seems strange to me because I was previously able to run this but then suddenly I cannot, I recently updated the GenomicSEM package so I don't know whether something changed that I haven't understood? 

I also wondered whether I am using too many variables in the larger analysis? It seems to work fine and ran through all of the calculations but then it just can't save the LDSC output (dimnames error above). 

I've definitely read the right number of variables into each section because for each part there are 121 variables so it cant be that one of the data points cannot be found.. 

Anyway I am probably overlooking something really simple so if you have any advice on this I'd be really grateful,

Thanks

Best wishes
Isabelle Foote

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Error in ldsc function and query r.e. variable quantity
parts:
Hi Isabelle, 

Thanks for bringing this up! Last week I put in an update to create a .log file for ldsc, but unfortunately only tested the scenario where trait.names were provided by the user for each trait, which was causing the new error when you left out the trait.names argument. I've updated the .ldsc code to name the .log file based on the munged summary stats files (and not the user provided trait.names), so you should be able to run your original code that does not include the trait.names argument without an error if you re-install Genomic SEM, restart R, and re-run. The reason it was throwing the error about dimnames is because trait.names is expecting a vector of how you want to name your traits with length equal to the number of traits you specify. So for 121 traits, it would be 121 manually provided trait.names (but again you do not have to provide this, it's just an option that can make it easier for specifying models in later steps because otherwise the traits will be named in the generic format of V1,V2,V3,...VX). 

For 121 variables in ldsc, you will run into a separate issue due to the package default of using 200 blocks for the jackknife procedure used to obtain standard errors and sampling covariances in ldsc. The specific problem is that using 200 blocks results in a singular sampling covariance (V) matrix for traits greater than 19 because the number of non-redundant elements in the genetic covariance matrix (S) is greater then the number of blocks used in the jackknife. We recently had another user that was trying to run a large set of variables, and for this application we added an argument to the ldsc function called n.blocks, which allows you to manually set the number of chunks used for the jackknife resampling. In order to avoid a singular V matrix, this number should be set to a value greater than the number of non-redundant elements in your genetic covariance matrix; in your case that number should be set to at least 7382. 

I want to highlight that jackknife resampling works by omitting one of the blocks in the genome, and then recomputing S. This is relevant to large numbers of traits because blocks should technically be independent of one another, so when using 7382 blocks you will almost certainly end up with a block being omitted that is in very high LD with an included block and therefore not independent of the included blocks. I don't have an overall sense yet of how much of a problem this actually is. However, using 2 traits with 7382 blocks I found that the standard errors were about .002 larger compared to using 200 blocks, so fairly minimal change and in the conservative direction. With that said, I think you would be safe enough to go ahead with using all 121 traits and setting the n.blocks argument to at least 7382 (you may just note it as a relatively minor limitation when writing things up). Let me know if anything is unclear of if you are still running into issues!

#calculate k non-redundant elements in 
#the genetic covariance matrix for 121 traits
k<-121*(121+1)/2

#run ldsc with n.blocks argument
LDSCoutput <- ldsc(traits, sample.prev, population.prev,ld,wld,trait.names,n.blocks=7382)

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Error in ldsc function and query r.e. variable quantity
parts:
Hi Isabelle, 

Thanks for bringing this up!! I hadn't thought about how large the file name was going to be when you have > 10 traits, and in your case it was exceeding a standard limit for file names (this was entirely separate from whether you were using the trait.names argument). I've updated the ldsc function so that it will either automatically truncate the file name when it is of a certain length so it doesn't throw the error you encountered, or I've added a new argument, ldsc.log, that can be used to provide your own name for the .log file. You definitely don't need to use this new argument, but if you were going to it would be written as below: 

LDSCoutput <- ldsc(traits, sample.prev, population.prev,ld,wld,trait.names,n.blocks=7382,ldsc.log="Isabelle")

Of course let me know if you have further issues and just to say I appreciate you uncovering some of the pieces where code is throwing opaque errors for a much larger sets of traits. If you end up getting any sort of counter-intuitive results, or wanted to share results over e-mail in general, from using the larger number of blocks that would definitely be clarifying just to see the behavior of the models for your particular application. 

Thanks!
 -Andrew
